summary: PowerShell code shows good set-strict-mode/error-handling practices; YAML uses pinned actions and least-privilege. Critical gaps: (1) Workflow expects test-results dir with fixtures but never creates them—collect step will fail without pre-committed files. (2) Task explicitly requires Pester tests, TDD approach, all tests via act, and act-result.txt artifact; none are provided/wired into workflow. (3) Parsing logic duplicated across JUnit/JSON converters (both validate→normalize→List[object]→return pattern, lines 30–90 and 101–160). (4) Workflow has no Pester invocation step, no fixture setup, no output validation against known-good values—incomplete for CI. Good: clear comments, good error messages, proper module structure.
